note: Re-judged 2026-10-31 (independent auditor, authored none of 7682a5dc93). RFC 5798 Section 7.2 says "The following operations MUST be performed when transmitting a VRRP packet: - Fill in the VRRP packet fields with the appropriate virtual router configuration state - Compute the VRRP checksum". 7682a5dc93 changed openV6 to open the RX socket on the instance MACVLAN instead of the parent (peer multicast with the shared virtual MAC is redirected to the PRIVATE macvlan); the TX socket still sets IPV6_CHECKSUM 6 (backend_linux.go), so on IPv6 the kernel still computes the checksum, and 0b9e085901 added panic boundaries only. The tagged units are byte-identical to the 2026-10-18 judgement: the fill clause and the opt-in IPv4 rfc5798-compatible checksum are proven by TestTransmittedAdvertFilledFromInstanceState, TestSendAdvertFillsFieldsAndChecksum, TestEncodeGoldenV3IPv4 and the TestBoundaryInterval negative, as the earlier overlay mutants showed. The IPv6 checksum clause remains unproven by any tagged unit: the transport test runs a fake backend whose IPv6 frame carries no checksum, and the IPv6 run of the instance test calls FillChecksum in the test body. Removing the IPV6_CHECKSUM setsockopt would leave every tagged unit green; only the integration-tagged QEMU units TestIntegrationOpenInstanceSocketOptions and TestIntegrationAdvertV6OnWire read it, and neither is tagged. Fix unchanged: tag one of them positive for this row and take its QEMU discrimination record. Verdict unchanged: weak.
